resource.title: NotebookLM VFS Integration and Client Enhancements
resource.prompt:
Complete the NotebookLM integration to make it act as an extension of the local Virtual File System (VFS).
Specific goals:
1. Extract names and metadata for both Sources and Studio Outputs (Notes, Audio Overviews, etc.) within a notebook.
2. For Studio Outputs, implement the ability to download their actual content (text for notes, audio for overviews).
3. Implement the ability to modify uploaded sources and move them between different notebooks.

Update the TypeScript client in agents/rsrch/src/notebooklm-client.ts and the CLI commands in agents/rsrch/src/commands/notebooklm.ts to support these new features. You can use the mock HTML files (like agents/rsrch/mocks/notebooklm-finDerivates.html) to understand the current NotebookLM DOM structure for Playwright interactions.

gitPatch.suggestedCommitMessage:
feat: expand NotebookLM integration with new actions and metadata

- Extract detailed source and artifact metadata, including parsing relative times to absolute and capturing `isSelected` states and `id`s.
- Implement `downloadArtifact` to support downloading both audio and extracted text contents depending on the artifact type (Note, Briefing, Timeline, etc.).
- Introduce `renameSource` and `selectSources` methods, parsing complex numerical ranges like `1-5,!3` for explicit, accurate selection directly mapped to UI indices.
- Extend `windmill-client.ts` with new trigger methods for these operations to securely manage asynchronous background tasks.
- Provide dedicated Windmill scripts for remotely wrapping `renameSource`, `selectSources`, and `downloadArtifact`.
- Update CLI commands in `commands/notebooklm.ts` to seamlessly dispatch commands directly to Windmill endpoints.

pullRequest.description:
This commit introduces the required features to interact deeply with NotebookLM content, supporting the orchestration needs of a local virtual file system proxy. It handles rich metadata scraping and remote-ready text artifact extraction logic alongside powerful source grouping controls.
